title: Want to Make Bolder Choices? Try Breathing Out Longer!
summary:
Have you ever felt nervous before a big decision? Maybe you had to choose between two things and weren't sure which was better. Well, here's a cool trick: try breathing out longer than you breathe in!

Scientists in Germany did a study with 41 people. They asked them to make risky choices while breathing normally or while breathing slowly with a long exhale (that's when you let air out). The ratio was 2 seconds in, 8 seconds out.

Guess what? When people breathed out longer, they made bolder choices! They were more focused on possible rewards and less worried about losing. But they still cared about losses — they just paid more attention to the good stuff.

The scientists also looked inside their brains using a special machine called an MRI. They saw more activity in parts of the brain that handle rewards and control the timing between heartbeats. So breathing out longer actually changes how your brain works!

Why does this happen? When you breathe out slowly, your heart rate slows down, and your brain gets a signal that it's safe to be a little more adventurous. It's like your body is saying, "Hey, everything's cool, let's go for it!"

This might sound like something from a yoga class, and you're right! Breathing techniques have been used for thousands of years in different cultures. Now science is showing they really work.

This could be super helpful for people who feel anxious or sad. Doctors might use breathing exercises to help them make better decisions. And who knows? Maybe it could even help you decide what to have for lunch... or whether to try that new skateboard trick!

So next time you're stuck on a choice, take a deep breath — and let it out slowly. It might just help you be a little braver!
why_it_matters: You can try this trick yourself before a test, a game, or any scary moment: breathe out longer and give your brain a 'you're safe' signal.
